description: Section 15 error names for the 50 terminal-index hostile mutations of MUTATIONS.tsv, written from the REM-PARITY text by an author who did not read the reference or its verifier. They were decided from byte-level descriptions under opaque ids, and are keyed here by the table's case_id.

filemark-missing.component: replica-a.bin (event: the filemark after replica A is absent; every byte unchanged)

tape_level.outcome: BotStructuralRecoveryRequired
tape_level.reason: No replica validates. A's records sit at their planned LBAs 25-27, but the read after its footer at LBA 28 returns AB's header instead of a Filemark, so A fails the trailing-filemark condition. Every later record moves down by one: AB occupies 28-30 with its filemark at 31, B 32-34 (planned 33), BC 36-38 (planned 37), C 40-42 (planned 41), and EOD is 44 (planned 45). B's header is not at its planned coordinate 33. C's footer, found from EOD at 42, records an observed footer LBA of 43, which the device contradicts. With A, B and C all invalid, Section 12.4 returns BotStructuralRecoveryRequired and the Section 8.4.1 walk.

quotes: The declared locations, the counts, and the trailing filemark agree with the device's measurements.
validate the header, footer and trailing filemark of every replica that layout plans
| `0x04` | 4 | trailing filemark count, exactly `1` |
A valid footer still does not prove its trailing filemark or any host-side commit record.

A Reader locates the frame from the immutable planned tuple, checks device-reported post-read positions for the addressed records and trailing filemark, and cross-checks the footer observation against that tuple.
TerminalIndexReplicaParse       replica framing or fixed-slot payload violates Section 8.3, 10.2–10.4, or 10.6
If A, B, and C all fail, the Scanner returns an explicit `BotStructuralRecoveryRequired` outcome and performs the Section 8.4.1 walk
filemark-missing.notes: Decided on the coordinator's clarified reading of the event. A's bytes are intact; the failure is the missing trailing filemark, which Section 8.3 plans as exactly one per component and Section 10.6 requires the device to confirm. In a BOT walk the same damage makes A and AB one tape file of 6 records, which fails the measured-count check of Section 12.3 item 2 ('A malformed frame or count mismatch is reported as a damaged terminal replica'), with the same name; Section 12.2 calls a missing trailing filemark structural damage. B and C also fail with TerminalIndexReplicaParse (displaced positions), and AB with TerminalIndexSeparationParse (its header is at LBA 28, not 29). None of these is a conflict: an invalid replica is degraded evidence (Section 8.5), and here no survivor remains.

The frame UUID (0x12 x 16) differs from the tape's UUID (0x11 x 16, the HMAC key the magic still matches), and the stale edition digest no longer recomputes, because tape_uuid is in its preimage. readings: Components are laid out as consecutive tape files, each followed by one filemark, as Section 8.3 plans. A component's records are its bytes taken 262144 at a time; a remainder forms a final short record.
Tape identity is the profile's tape UUID (0x11 x 16), which is also the HMAC key of every role magic.
An invalid separation extent never changes the Scanner's inventory; 'degraded' is used only as Section 12.6 uses it, for missing or invalid replicas.
